newsitem.title: UK: Norway's Karsto loses two days LPG output - Statoil.
newsitem.headline: Norway's Karsto loses two days LPG output - Statoil.

text.p: Norwegian state oil company Statoil said on Friday that it lost two days worth of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) production from its Karsto terminal this week due to a crude supply hitch.

"I can confirm that we have declared force majeure," said a Statoil spokeswoman, without giving further details. "There is a two-day delay in production, but it is not a big loss. Very few customers will notice."
She said that delays to crude oil liftings at the Statfjord and Gullfaks fields due to bad weather in late March caused the production cutback.
Karsto produces 5,000 tonnes a day of propane and 2,500 tonnes a day of butane.
The spokeswoman said that the problem did not affect natural gas processing as enough supplies were held in storage.
